claim: Reject ruin and hidden concavity first, then evaluate whether a payoff is robust or positively convex after liquidity, tail pricing and execution friction.
Stress payoff convexity and absorbing barriers under extreme but explicit states.
Compare realized tails with the surface after bid-ask and event coverage.
Reject any return thesis with an unresolved absorbing loss state.
Reject hidden concavity whose tail loss is not strictly bounded.
Reject an options edge that does not survive executable round-trip costs.
Excluded claim: directional target prices attributed to the named author
Excluded claim: missing volatility facts filled by model memory
Known limit: Empirica and private trading positions, sizing and execution are not public.
Known limit: Published philosophical claims do not automatically define numerical option thresholds; calibration must remain separately labeled.
